title: 7. Trend story pipeline (XL)
description:
Shipped story: ship-2fd025 (AI trend stories). Size XL. Depends on stories 1, 4 and 5.

As an editor, I want trend stories drafted from knowledge signals, so that the map has stories I only have to approve.

Acceptance criteria:
- Flow: knowledge snapshot, AI draft citing signals, Proposal (story draft), editor approval of the copy and of a figure drawn from map data.
- Every claim in a draft traces to a cited signal; an uncited claim blocks submission.
- Drafting uses GPT-6 Luna.
- Attribution reads AI.
- Nothing is published without editor approval.
- All behaviour here ships with Gherkin specs (Feature/Scenario/Given/When/Then) in the repo, written first and green before close.

comments.text: Trend-story path built: PR #690 (feat/idea-trend-stories), merged to develop at c50b6fd6 after CI (ts, python, smoke) passed. Not on main, no release, no deploy, no live run or live LLM call. Adds papyrus ideas trends --site KEY --snapshot PATH|URL [--store proposals] [--dry-run] [--max N]: signals from the weekly knowledge snapshot without a model, one GPT-6 Luna call, a deterministic citation check (each sentence cites a snapshot signal; its numbers and dates come from the signals it cites; failing drafts are not filed and the run record says why), story_draft Proposals in draft with proposer AI, targets = cited clusters/entities, evidence.figure = line-chart spec of the cited signals' weekly counts for the editor to approve with the copy. Dedupe on same targets (skipped under IAM, recorded), one soft review per run, works with PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_AUTH=iam and as an editor. The reader-actions function now keeps a validated evidence.figure, so a site needs a backend deploy with this release before the figure is stored. Specs: features_backend/idea-trend-stories.feature, proposals.feature; tests test_idea_trends.py. Docs: docs/idea-pipeline.md#trend-stories. Remaining: first real dry run against Shipped's latest snapshot (needs Ryan: OPENAI_API_KEY and an IAM or editor session), Shipped backend deploy, scheduling.
